stored_ideas.name: Population-Linked Supply
stored_ideas.description: Token supply expands and contracts with oracle-reported changes in verified global population. Each epoch, an oracle committee reports births, deaths, and net migration; the protocol mints or burns supply proportional to the reported delta. This is Experiment #001 (MASTER BUILD PROMPT §25): the lab must attempt to prove or disprove it, NOT assume it is a good idea.

stored_ideas.name: Homeostatic Reserve Stablecoin
stored_ideas.description: A stable-value unit whose reserve policy is modeled on biological homeostasis: like an organism's negative-feedback loops (blood glucose, body temperature), the mechanism holds value near its target not through one peg-breaking act, but through layered counteracting responses of graded strength. Step by step: (1) the unit targets a 1.00 reference value against its reference basket; (2) the FIRST-LAYER response is a transfer-fee rebate/penalty: when the market price deviates within ±0.5%, redemption fees rise and minting fees fall (or vice versa), nudging arbitrageurs to push value back — cheap, fast, weak; (3) the SECOND-LAYER response activates beyond ±0.5%: the reserve pool's yield distribution tilts — the excess return from over-collateralized reserves flows to whichever side of the market needs shrinking (buyers when below peg to reward contractionary pressure, redeemers when above peg), a stronger, slower correction funded by real reserve yield; (4) the THIRD-LAYER response activates beyond ±2%: issuance is throttled by a mint-holiday that deterministically scales new supply creation down as |deviation| grows, and a portion of the protocol's own insurance tranche is used for direct open-market rebalancing; (5) crucially, each layer DEACTIVATES as deviation shrinks, and the layers' thresholds are fixed by rule, not discretion; (6) the reserve ratio itself floats within a [1.05, 1.30] band, and when the ratio hits the band's floor, the second layer's yield redirection automatically pauses — the biological insight that an exhausted organ must rest rather than respond — preventing a death spiral where yield payments drain the last collateral.

stored_ideas.name: Fee-Relay Escrow Market
stored_ideas.description: An escrowed relay market for transaction fees that lets payers lock tomorrow's fee at today's price, with relayers competing to execute. Step by step: (1) a payer wanting a transaction included in a future window posts an escrowed fee voucher: the amount they are willing to pay, the deadline window, and a slippage tolerance; (2) relayers (anyone) can accept the voucher by posting a performance bond; (3) when the transaction is confirmed on-chain within the window, the voucher releases min(actual fee at inclusion time, voucher amount) to the relayer who shepherded it and refunds the remainder to the payer; (4) if the deadline passes unconfirmed, the relayer's bond partially compensates the payer for the missed window at a fixed rate; (5) the market clearing happens through posted vouchers, not auctions — relayers see the full book and pick the vouchers whose (amount, deadline, risk) profile matches their blockspace inventory; (6) the escrow is a deterministic contract: no relayer ever holds the payer's funds, and the bond insures execution risk instead of a trusted intermediary.

stored_ideas.name: Corridor-Native FX Batch Matching
stored_ideas.description: A batch-matching mechanism for cross-currency settlement that replaces continuous pairwise AMMs with periodic batch auctions keyed to trade corridors. Step by step: (1) participants submit limit orders for currency pairs along defined corridors (e.g., USD-stable ↔ EUR-stable ↔ GBP-stable); (2) settlement happens in discrete batches (e.g., every 30 seconds): within a batch, the mechanism computes a uniform clearing price per corridor via a deterministic volume-matching rule (all orders crossing the clearing price execute at that single price); (3) cross-corridor matching is allowed: an order EUR→GBP can clear through the USD corridor if the combined EUR→USD→GBP path prices better than the direct pair, making thin direct pairs liquid through path composition; (4) batch-level surplus (the spread between submitted limits and clearing prices) accrues to the NEXT batch's fee rebate pool instead of to an operator — the mechanism itself has no fee take; (5) a stability condition is enforced deterministically: if any corridor's batch volume falls below a floor, that corridor merges into its parent corridor (the deepest adjacent path) so liquidity never fragments into uneconomic thin pairs; (6) pricing within a batch is a pure matching computation over signed orders — no state carried between batches except the rebate pool.

stored_ideas.name: Countercyclical Corridor Insurance Float
stored_ideas.description: A corridor-level insurance float that supplies liquidity exactly when batch FX corridors thin out. Step by step: (1) LPs stake into a corridor float pool and receive float tokens; premium income accrues continuously from corridors that borrow float liquidity. (2) Each corridor's rebate pool (from the §16 batch matcher's surplus recycling) pays a premium stream proportional to how far its rolling volume falls below its merge floor — thin, stressed corridors pay more, exactly like insurance. (3) When a corridor's volume drops below its floor, the float automatically lends inventory into that corridor's next batches (as additional clearing inventory), dampening the price-band pressure the thin corridor would otherwise exert. (4) As corridor volume recovers past the floor, borrowed inventory returns to the float plus the accrued premium. (5) Float LPs earn premium + a share of corridor surplus in calm periods; the insurance pays out in stressed ones. The control-surface feed: the insurance family's premium schedule is driven BY the market family's own volume-floor state, and the float's inventory injection acts ON the market family's clearing-price band.

stored_ideas.name: Escrowed Batch-Clearing Insurance Pool
stored_ideas.description: An insurance pool that guarantees batch-auction clearing when solvers fail or withhold: (1) settlement participants escrow a small premium fraction alongside each order into a corridor-level insurance pool. (2) A solver that wins a batch posts a performance bond; if its batch settles late, partially, or optimality-fraudulently, the pool instantly steps in as a fallback solver of last resort using its escrowed inventory. (3) The insurance premium each participant pays is state-dependent: it RISES with the corridor's recent solver-concentration (fewer active solvers = more fragile batches = pricier insurance), so the insurance price itself is a real-time fragility sensor the corridor can act on. (4) Pool LPs earn premiums plus surplus-share in normal operation; the pool only draws down on solver failure events. (5) When solver concentration returns to healthy levels (measured as a long EMA of distinct bonded solvers), premiums fall back — countercyclical pricing in BOTH directions.

stored_ideas.name: Prediction-Weighted Corridor Risk Pricing
stored_ideas.description: Corridor risk is priced by a prediction market instead of a committee: (1) a continuous prediction market trades binary 'corridor-stress' contracts — will corridor X thin below its floor within N batches? (2) The corridor's insurance premium (paid by corridor operators to a float) is set BY the market odds: premium = base + k * market-implied stress probability, updated each batch. (3) The market's traders — anyone with information about payment-flow patterns, seasonal corridors, or counterparty risk — are paid to be right early: their odds move premiums before the stress arrives, giving corridors lead time to top up inventory or pre-arrange routing. (4) When stress events resolve, the market settles against the corridor's own on-chain volume state (no oracle: settlement reads the floor state directly). (5) The float that receives premiums is capitalized by LPs; the prediction market is the pricing surface, the float is the balance sheet.

stored_ideas.name: Dual-Sided Bond Auction Rebalancer
stored_ideas.description: A rebalancing mechanism for performance-bond markets where bond SUPPLY is auctioned on both sides of the risk: (1) solver bonds (the insurance family's strike-disarming capital) are auctioned periodically — solvers bid the fee they accept for being bonded; the auction clears at the market price of bonded-ness. (2) Simultaneously, corridor insurance tranches (the float's coverage) are auctioned on the demand side — participants bid for coverage, clearing at the market price of guarantee. (3) The two clears are LINKED by a rebalancing rule: when the bonded-ness price (supply side) exceeds the coverage price (demand side), the auction mints more bonds (more solver capacity, cheaper coverage); when coverage price exceeds bonded-ness, the auction retires bonds (capacity tightens, coverage dearer) — a two-sided market that finds the equilibrium capacity for the guarantee stack rather than setting it by committee. (4) The rebalancing is state-dependent through the same EMA fragility signal: thinning solver sets trigger retirement (concentration risk prices itself into higher coverage costs), and the coverage premium's rise recapitalizes the pool automatically. (5) Settlement of both auction sides is native on-chain: bond state and tranche state are both deterministic.

stored_ideas.name: Tranche-Segmented Settlement Guarantee Stack
stored_ideas.description: A two-layer capital structure for settlement guarantees where risk is tranched instead of pooled flat: (1) settlement participants buy guarantee coverage in SENIOR tranches — first-loss capital from the float's calm-period surplus, priced cheap, covering routine solver hiccups (latency straddles, marginal degradations — the frequent small failures). (2) LPs seeking yield underwrite JUNIOR tranches — the fallback-solver inventory and its bonds — earning concentration-priced premiums from the batch-clearing pool, covering the rare big failures (solver strikes, correlated exits). (3) The tranche boundary is itself dynamic: it is set by the prediction market's implied stress odds — when implied stress rises, the senior/junior split point moves so MORE capital is pre-committed to the junior (event) layer before the event arrives, converting the market's early warning into a capital reallocation the pool could never do by committee. (4) Premiums flow tranchewise: senior coverage pays a steady fee into the float's surplus; junior underwriting earns the state-dependent fragility premium; both are priced off the SAME implied-odds surface so there is one coherent risk price across the stack. (5) On failure events: senior absorbs first (routine), junior activates the fallback solver (severe); on calm, premiums recapitalize senior first (rebuilding the cheap layer).

stored_ideas.name: Vol-Weighted Fee Smoothing Escrow
stored_ideas.description: An escrow that converts realized fee volatility into smoothing inventory for the fee-relay voucher market: (1) payers buying fee vouchers pay a small vol-weight (a premium proportional to the CURRENT measured fee volatility, not a fixed spread). (2) The vol-weights accumulate into a smoothing inventory that the escrow deploys when realized fees exceed voucher faces: instead of rationing (the round-2 finding — acceptance collapses during spikes), the smoothing inventory tops up relayer margins exactly when G_t rises, making acceptance INCREASING in congestion (the v2 congestion-indexed premium, now capitalized by the market's own vol payments rather than a parameter). (3) When volatility subsides, the smoothing inventory decays back into rebates for loyal voucher holders — the calm-period surplus share. (4) The measured volatility input is a long EMA of realized inclusion fees (native on-chain data), so the weight is manipulation-resistant by the same window lineage the lab has reused three times. (5) The design closes the loop the round-2 model left open: the acceptance equation's k_premium term is no longer a hopeful parameter but a capitalized budget.

stored_ideas.name: Vol-Weighted Fee Smoothing Escrow
stored_ideas.description: Batch transactions pay into an escrowed fee pool. A volatility-weighted drawdown rule converts measured anchor volatility into a retention fraction and a release rate, smoothing effective fees across volatility regimes without a trusted price feed.

stored_ideas.name: Tranche-Segmented Settlement Guarantee Stack
stored_ideas.description: A settlement guarantee stack prices each tranche's exposure per batch; a deterministic solvency rule reallocates guarantee fees across tranches when queued exposure grows, keeping total capitalization matched to total exposure.

stored_ideas.name: Homeostatic Reserve Stablecoin
stored_ideas.description: The stablecoin's controller reads the anchor level and its delta, computes a mean-reversion pressure, and sets issuance and reserve requirements homeostatically — contraction under deviation, expansion under convergence.

stored_ideas.name: Dual-Sided Bond Auction Rebalancer
stored_ideas.description: Each rebalancing round runs a dual-sided auction: capacity is set by seasoning depth, the sell side clears at the bid, the buy side at the ask, and realized slippage feeds back into the next round's capacity.

stored_ideas.name: Escrowed Batch-Clearing Insurance Pool
stored_ideas.description: Batched claims split the bill across exposure-weighted partitions of an escrowed pool; a solvency tie defers clearing when the float is short, forcing explicit re-capitalization instead of silent overdraft.

stored_ideas.name: Corridor-Native FX Batch Matching
stored_ideas.description: FX corridor orders batch-clear against posted two-sided escrow; the impact check defers oversized batches and the rebate pool compensates posted inventory from captured spread.

stored_ideas.name: Fee-Spike Mutual for Rollup Batches
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: protocols posting transactions on a shared rollup subscribe to a batch-fee mutual, paying a premium per block window. Step 2: the mutual prices premiums from the realized distribution of batch settlement fees over a trailing window (e.g. the 95th-percentile fee level). Step 3: when the next window's settlement fee exceeds the subscribed band, the mutual reimburses the excess above the band cap. Step 4: unused premium accumulates in a reserve tranche that absorbs spike payouts before mutual members are rationed pro-rata. Step 5: reserve levels are published per window so members can exit or top up on transparent data.

stored_ideas.name: Drawdown-Underwritten Liquidity Corridor
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: an FX corridor pool pairs ordinary liquidity with opt-in underwriter liquidity. Step 2: ordinary LPs earn the spread; underwriters earn the spread plus an insurance premium quoted from realized corridor drawdown statistics. Step 3: if corridor depth depletes past a drawdown band, underwriter liquidity converts to trading liquidity at a pre-agreed conversion price, absorbing the tail. Step 4: as realized drawdowns deepen, the premium ticks up at a published schedule. Step 5: when the corridor refills, underwriters are made whole first from spread revenue.

stored_ideas.name: Counter-Cyclical Fee Sink Insurer
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: the protocol routes a configurable share of fee revenue into an insurer sink during low-volatility regimes. Step 2: regime detection is deterministic: realized fee volatility below its trailing median opens the accumulation tap. Step 3: during high-volatility regimes, the sink disburses to cap the effective fee paid by small senders, paying the difference to validators. Step 4: the tap and cap rates follow a published schedule keyed to the volatility percentile. Step 5: sink solvency is reported each epoch.

stored_ideas.name: Relay Congestion Cover Mesh
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: relay and RPC operators join a cover mesh, staking a deposit and declaring served routes. Step 2: route congestion is attested from operator-reported plus client-side measurements, aggregated per interval. Step 3: operators whose routes exceed a congestion band draw compensation from the mesh to fund burst capacity, paid from the mesh premium pool. Step 4: premiums are re-priced from the realized congestion distribution of the previous interval, so chronically congested routes cost more to insure. Step 5: operators with sustained over-reporting discrepancies lose staking priority.

stored_ideas.name: Volatility-Sized Settlement Escrow
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: FX settlement counterparties lock funds in an escrow whose cover tranche is dynamically sized from realized pair-volatility. Step 2: underwriters fund the cover tranche and receive a premium paid from the settlement spread. Step 3: if either party defaults inside the settlement window, the cover tranche completes the leg, up to its sized cap. Step 4: the tranche size re- targets each window from the trailing realized volatility of the pair, so turbulent pairs must carry proportionally more cover. Step 5: unclaimed premiums compound into the tranche, lowering the spread in calm regimes.

stored_ideas.name: Forecast-Indexed Fee Smoothing Pool
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a fee smoothing pool holds a buffer of protocol fee revenue. Step 2: a prediction market runs continuous no-limit book auctions on the proposition 'median fee next epoch exceeds threshold T', with resolution by on-chain fee statistics. Step 3: the pool's smoothing intensity — how much buffer it injects or absorbs per epoch — is keyed to the implied congestion probability from that market rather than to spot congestion. Step 4: traders who stake the forecast wrong fund the buffer that compensates traders who face the realized outcome. Step 5: the pool publishes the implied probability and its action each epoch.

stored_ideas.name: Prediction-Settled Hashprice Hedge Board
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: compute suppliers (or AI-inference providers) post long/short positions on forward hashprice-equivalent compute price boards. Step 2: boards settle against a median of reported realized compute prices from registered suppliers, making the settlement reference a market statistic rather than a single oracle. Step 3: margin is marked to realized volatility of the settlement reference; volatile reference periods raise required margin deterministically. Step 4: suppliers whose realized revenue falls below their hedged band draw from counterparties' margin. Step 5: the board publishes the reference series and margin schedule.

stored_ideas.name: Consensus-Odds Liquidity Rebate
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: an exchange allocates a share of its taker-fee revenue to a rebate pool for makers. Step 2: alongside order books, a lightweight prediction book trades 'next-window volume will exceed V' with binary settlement from exchange-published volume. Step 3: makers earn rebate multipliers when their quoted depth persists through windows the forecast market priced as high-demand. Step 4: the multiplier schedule is published per implied probability bucket, so deep quotes during forecast demand earn more than quotes in forecast slack. Step 5: the forecast book's losing side funds part of the rebate pool.

stored_ideas.name: Adverse-Selection Taxed Prediction Clearing
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a prediction-clearing venue for tokenized claims charges a spread set from realized order-flow imbalance statistics. Step 2: when realized imbalance indicates informed flow (persistent one-sided pressure with subsequent reference moves), the spread widens deterministically for the aggressing side. Step 3: proceeds from the widened spread fund a liquidity-incentive pool paid to balanced two-sided flow. Step 4: the venue publishes the imbalance statistics and the spread schedule. Step 5: reference resolution uses the market's own time-weighted mid rather than last trade, bounding settlement manipulation.

stored_ideas.name: Belief-Weighted Volatility Target Fund
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a fund tracks a volatility target for its exposure to a basket of protocol assets. Step 2: prediction markets on future realized volatility (bucketed ranges) trade continuously; the fund holds small stakes that pay out when volatility lands in extreme buckets. Step 3: the fund's risk engine blends realized volatility with the market-implied bucket probabilities to set exposure. Step 4: when implied probability of stress buckets rises, the fund de-risks before realized volatility confirms the move, funded partly by the prediction payouts. Step 5: the blend weights and exposures are published per rebalance.

stored_ideas.name: Disagreement-Weighted Oracle Quorum
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a stablecoin's reference exchange rate is fed by a quorum of independent oracle reporters. Step 2: each reporter also posts a stake into a disagreement market on the proposition 'the quorum median next interval deviates from my report by more than d'. Step 3: reporters whose reports are confirmed outliers against the realized median lose stake to the quorum's accuracy pool; reporters who correctly flagged their own potential deviation keep rewards. Step 4: reports are weighted by the trailing disagreement-market calibration of each reporter, down-weighting persistently mis-calibrated feeds without governance votes. Step 5: the median, weights, and calibration scores are published per interval.

stored_ideas.name: Prediction-Fee Fallback Oracle
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a payment rail reads a primary price feed for FX conversion, with a declared staleness budget. Step 2: if the primary feed goes stale, a fallback ladder activates: first a secondary quorum, then a time-decayed prediction market quote that has been trading continuously on the same conversion rate. Step 3: each fallback level charges a progressively higher conversion fee, paid into an insurance pool for payment senders. Step 4: the prediction market quote is only used if its open interest exceeds a floor, bounding thin-book manipulation. Step 5: when the primary feed resumes, the fee ladder resets and the pool settles accrued cover.

stored_ideas.name: Report-Bonded Forecast Fee Meter
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a rollup's fee meter is set from a feed of attested batch-fee levels. Step 2: feed reporters post bonds into a forecast market on the next interval's median batch fee, bucketed into fee bands. Step 3: the meter uses the bucket with the highest bonded probability as its operating band, and adjusts posting requirements for applications inside that band. Step 4: reporters whose bonds land in the wrong bucket forfeit them to the meter's stabilization pool, which compensates applications caught above their band. Step 5: band selection and pool balance publish per interval.

stored_ideas.name: Attestation-Locked Prediction Settlement
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: prediction markets on payment-flow outcomes (e.g. 'crossrail volume next window exceeds V') settle against attested aggregate flows from registered payment operators. Step 2: each operator's attestation is bound to a settlement bond, slashed on divergence from the cross-attested median. Step 3: settlement of the prediction market waits for a quorum of operator attestations plus a challenge window; any bond-backed challenger can dispute with a corrected attestation. Step 4: slashing proceeds fund the market's liquidity incentives, aligning operator honesty with market depth. Step 5: the attested series is published with each settlement.

stored_ideas.name: Dual-Quote Stability Insurance Market
stored_ideas.description: Step 1: a stablecoin maintains primary stability via its existing mechanism (e.g. collateral + redemption). Step 2: an always-on prediction book trades the proposition 'next epoch's dual-quote peg deviation — median of two independent oracles — exceeds b', with bounded position sizes. Step 3: epoch-end fees route a share to the book's liquidity when the peg holds, so the insurance market is paid in calm regimes. Step 4: if the dual-quote deviation exceeds b, book payouts fund a peg support tranche that absorbs de-peg redemptions at the bounded rate. Step 5: the tranche refills from book liquidity incentives in the next calm regime.
